subject: Service assurance template — baseline uptime, p95 latency ceilings & exception runway
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmecorp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com, ops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2025-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft SLA redlines and question on monthly remedy runway

Hi Marissa / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've circulated Redwood's standard SLA with legal and ops and attached a redlined PDF with two asks that need clarity before procurement can move forward:

1) A request to raise the baseline uptime guarantee to 99.98% (current template: 99.95%).
2) A requirement that monthly service credits be able to roll forward for 90 days rather than expire monthly (they'd like an "exception runway" to smooth billing impact during spikes).

Operations also flagged p95 latency language — they want a firm 200ms p95 for text-generation routes used in production, and an explicit carveout for scheduled maintenance windows tied to a region-level maintenance calendar.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can reasonably accept either change, or propose alternative guardrails (e.g., higher credit caps, conditional uptime tiers, or maintenance blackout notice windows)? Jordan has been looped in on ops details.

Attachments: Acme_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf (redlines)

Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Operations | Acme Analytics

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-05T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA redlines and question on monthly remedy runway

Jordan —

Appreciate the detailed redlines and the clarity on the ops ask. We're keen to get Acme to production quickly; Ben and I discussed this morning and wanted to align internally with Legal before responding. High-level notes here so you have visibility while we finalize a formal response:

- Baseline uptime: 99.98% is aggressive relative to our standard hosted offering; our template is 99.95% with an operational model that includes proactive monitoring, regional failover, and availability runbooks.
- Rolling credits: we understand the concern about billing volatility — we're open to a 60-day roll-forward on credits for the first 6 months of the contract as a pilot, combined with a cap on total monthly remedial credits.
- Latency (p95): 200ms p95 for text-generation in production depends heavily on request patterns and model choice. We can guarantee 200ms p95 for inference on our smaller generation profile (gpt-lite-1) at your expected QPS, but would need to test on your actual workload.
- Maintenance carveouts: we can formalize a maintenance calendar and provide 72-hour advance notice for planned regional windows; emergency maintenance would be governed by a narrower carveout.

I'll loop Laura (Legal) and Ben (Account lead) for a proposed language patch and a single-sheet summary of trade-offs (uptime delta vs. credit cap). Expect a formal doc by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-06T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA redlines and question on monthly remedy runway

Team —

Quick internal run-through after Marissa's note. Propose the following compromise language we can offer Acme to preserve economics while addressing their ask:

- Uptime: Offer a phased uptime uplift to 99.98% for the first 12 months but with a conditional availability pool: if sustained usage > X GPUs or >Y requests/minute for two consecutive billing cycles, we revert to 99.95% while we scale Dedicated capacity. This protects us from under-provisioning risk.

- Credits: Allow credits to roll forward for 60 days (pilot) and offer an optional one-time 90-day roll-forward if Acme purchases a 6-month credit buffer (prepaid credit escrow). Cap total monthly credits at 30% of monthly invoice.

- Latency: Commit to 200ms p95 on a specified endpoint (gpt-lite-1) after a 2-week performance validation during onboarding; if traffic patterns deviate from the tested profile we convert the SLO to a best-effort target with defined escalation rules and compensating credits if missed.

- Maintenance: 72-hour planned notice; emergency maintenance allowed with a defined narrow carveout (and we agree to post-incident RCA and up to one goodwill credit per quarter in case of unplanned downtime > 2 hours).

Laura — can you run a quick redline to reflect conditional uptime rollback language and the credit escrow option? Rishi — pinging you for an ops feasibility check on the 2-week validation and the conditional scaling thresholds.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Director | Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmecorp.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: 2025-10-07T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed SLA language & attachments (pilot exceptions and credit escrow)

Jordan / Acme team —

Attached is a proposed redline to your PDF and a clean copy of Redwood's suggested contract language: "Redwood-Proposed-SLA-2025-10-07.docx". Summary of the concrete offers in the draft:

1) Uptime: Phased uplift to 99.98% for an initial 12-month period, subject to conditional rollback to 99.95% if utilization exceeds scaling thresholds for two consecutive billing periods. Conditional rollback includes a 30-day notice and shared runbook for migration to Dedicated capacity.

2) Rolling Credits: 60-day roll-forward on monthly credits for the first six months as a pilot. Option to convert to a 90-day roll-forward if Acme elects a prepaid credit escrow equivalent to one month's average usage. Monthly credit cap set to 30% of invoice.

3) Latency SLOs: 200ms p95 guaranteed for the designated text-generation endpoint after an onboarding performance validation (14 days). If post-validation traffic characteristics differ materially, the SLO reverts to a target with an agreed remediation path and credits if failure persists beyond defined windows.

4) Maintenance: Planned maintenance will have 72-hour notice. Emergency maintenance carveouts limited to operationally necessary events; each emergency event will be accompanied by an RCA within 5 business days and a one-time goodwill credit if outage > 2 hours.

Next steps: if this aligns, please confirm (a) acceptance of the 60-day pilot runway, or (b) interest in the prepaid escrow to expand to 90 days, and (c) whether ops wants us to run a short validation on a representative production trace next week.

Attachments: Redwood-Proposed-SLA-2025-10-07.docx (proposed clause text)

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
